chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, who said:

I wrote to him asking him: O my master, it has been narrated from your grandfather that he said: 'There is no harm in a man praying the night prayer at the beginning of the night.' He wrote back: 'At whatever time he prays, it is permissible, if God wills.'
ai.seo_question: When is the best time to pray the night prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This correspondence from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the jurisprudential flexibility (rukhsah) in Shia tradition regarding the timing of Salat al-Layl, moving beyond strict early-night preferences to validate any portion of the night. The Imam’s concise reply underscores the principle that the spiritual merit of the prayer is not contingent upon a specific temporal window, provided it is performed within the night hours. This reflects the broader Shia emphasis on accessibility in voluntary acts of worship, encouraging consistent devotion rather than rigid adherence to specific times.
